authorized_edits: Move the read of data before the free() in the bad sink, or remove the free()-then-read ordering; no other behaviour may change.
Allow up to 128 bytes of added x86-64 code in a gate-3-verified unused region of a loadable R-X segment; zero bytes alone are not evidence.
Allow no new segment, dynamic import, GOT/PLT/relocation edit or permission broadening.
environment_assumptions: glibc may reuse the freed 100-byte chunk and overwrite its first bytes, which is why the defect path is observable without a sanitizer; this is not a language guarantee
CET: ENDBR64 is compile-time only; runtime IBT/shadow-stack enforcement is not verified
forbidden_behavior: read a heap block after free() has released it (the --uaf path)
invalid_behavior: the --uaf path frees the block and then reads it; the read must return the original 99 'A' bytes, never allocator metadata
valid_behavior: the good path runs goodG2B then goodB2G, each printing the 99-byte payload once, and exits 0
valid_domain: argv[1] is accepted but not read by the sinks; the upstream case allocates malloc(100), fills 99 bytes with 'A' and terminates with NUL
